title_en: Spencer Look and Jack VanDerhei: The Assumptions That Can Put Your Retirement at Risk
title_zh: Spencer Look 与 Jack VanDerhei：那些可能让你的退休陷入风险的假设
subtitle_zh: 两位Morningstar退休专家拆解社保改革、长期护理与寿命三大不确定假设
summary_zh: 本期The Long View由主持人Amy Arnott与Christine Benz对话Morningstar退休与政策研究中心的两位嘉宾：退休研究副总监Spencer Look与总监Jack VanDerhei。两人围绕「美国是否真的存在退休危机」给出了比舆论更平衡的判断：其模型显示约40%到45%的人口面临退休资金短缺风险，但缺口高度集中于低收入劳动者、单身女性以及黑人和西班牙裔家庭，而持续储蓄、按计划参与的人往往状况良好。他们强调三个最不确定、也最容易被忽视的假设——长期护理、寿命与社会保障改革。长期护理的影响巨大：若忽略它，资金短缺率会从40%—45%降到约25%；但许多研究把它假设掉，寄望Medicaid兜底或家人无偿照护，这既不现实也非客户所愿，正确做法是用情景分析与敏感性测试去逼近，而非套用单一数字。在社保方面，按2032年10月受托人报告的排期，所有人默认将面临22%的福利削减，年长者已无足够时间靠401(k)补足，必须借助压力测试、推迟退休等安排应对。对计划设计，他们主张别只盯着平均效应，而要聚焦「高风险人群」，通过自动加入、较高默认递延率、自动递增与管理账户等组合真正改善结果。这期节目为顾问与个人提供了一套把不确定性纳入退休规划的可操作框架。

turns.zh: 你听到我这么说不会意外——我真的很喜欢关于长期护理（long-term care）的讨论。Spencer和Jack都得出结论：退休规划界低估了长期护理作为人们退休计划风险因素的分量，所以我很乐意深入探讨这一点。好，那我们进入正题。

The Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies actually started about four and a half years ago and what it is is a center that allows us to provide empirical evidence
turns.zh: 这个中心最初是怎么成立的？你们想完成的使命是什么？Spencer，如果你不介意的话，我先来说。Morningstar退休与政策研究中心其实是大约四年半前成立的，它是一个能让我们提供实证证据（empirical evidence）的中心，

turns.en: that lets policymakers, plan sponsors and other stakeholders understand the trade offs in terms of proposal legislation, proposed regulation, and different types of plan designs. So instead of just coming up with a single headline number, we provide very, very detailed information.
turns.zh: ……让政策制定者、计划发起方（plan sponsors）和其他利益相关方，理解拟议立法、拟议法规以及不同类型计划设计之间的取舍。所以我们不只是给出一个单一的头条数字，而是提供非常非常详细的信息。

turns.en: Spencer, I'm wondering if you can talk about one of the linch pens of the work that you to do at the Center, the Morningstar model of U.S. retirement outcomes. Can you talk about how it works and what makes it different for more traditional retirement analyses? Yes, I love this question.
turns.zh: Spencer，我想请你谈谈你们在中心工作的一大支柱——Morningstar美国退休结果模型（Morningstar model of U.S. retirement outcomes）。你能讲讲它是怎么运作的，以及它跟更传统的退休分析有何不同吗？好，我很喜欢这个问题。

turns.en: The model that you just referenced, that's our flagship model for the Center, powers a lot of the work that we do. It is a household level micro simulation model, think a monocaloid type of approach for the audience out there. We built this on top of a government survey, the survey of consumer finances, which is
turns.zh: 你刚提到的那个模型，是我们中心的旗舰模型，支撑着我们做的很多工作。它是一个家庭层面的微观模拟模型（micro simulation model）——对在场的听众来说，可以想成一种蒙特卡洛（Monte Carlo）式的方法。我们把它建立在一项政府调查之上，即消费者财务状况调查（Survey of Consumer Finances），它……

turns.en: a representative sample of the U.S. population. And then we model, you know, project as people go forward and work, do their career, kind of go into retirement. We are very granular with what we're doing, kind of echoing what Jack was saying with the mission and kind of goal of the center.
turns.zh: ……是一个能代表美国人口的样本。然后我们进行建模、预测：随着人们往前走、工作、经历职业生涯、逐步进入退休。我们做得非常细致，这也呼应了Jack所说的中心的使命和目标。

turns.en: We incorporate people's wages, savings, job changes, you know, upon job change. Do they cash out their retirement plan? We reflect pre-retirement with draws. Of course, moving into retirement, we incorporate social security, spending models, longevity, long-term care.
turns.zh: 我们纳入了人们的工资、储蓄、换工作的情况——换工作时他们会不会把退休计划里的钱取现？我们反映了退休前的取款。当然，进入退休后，我们纳入社会保障、支出模型、寿命（longevity）、长期护理。

turns.en: It's a very detailed model that goes through a lot of this really messiness in the reality to, you know, produce a distribution of outcomes on retirement and chromatic listed. So the goal here is to analyze retirement and chromatic listed. We don't just stop at, you know, a wealth balance of a replacement rate.
turns.zh: 这是一个非常细致的模型，它穿过现实中大量的这种「乱麻」，从而产出关于退休和经济充足性（economic adequacy）结果的分布。所以这里的目标是分析退休的经济充足性，我们不会只停在一个财富余额或替代率（replacement rate）上。

turns.en: We use that approach to kind of look at how likely it is people can run short of money in retirement. The really big differentiator for us is leaning into the behavior. So instead of assuming people follow a set schedule, you know, they always save 5%, 6%, just as a simple example, our frameworks are going to be dynamic.
turns.zh: 我们用这套方法去考察人们在退休后钱不够用的可能性有多大。对我们来说真正的差异化之处，在于侧重行为（behavior）本身。所以我们不假设人们遵循一个固定的时间表——比如总是存5%、6%，这只是个简单例子——我们的框架是动态的。

turns.en: They change and reflect as people have a new job, a new type of plan as they, you know, make more money. And older, very clearly empirical data shows that, you know, people's behaviors can change. So we're reflecting that in our framework and I think that's what really differentiates us with our modeling approach.
turns.zh: 它会随着人们换了一份新工作、一种新类型的计划、赚更多的钱、变老而改变并做出反映。非常明确的实证数据显示，人们的行为是会变的。所以我们在框架中反映了这一点，我认为这正是我们的建模方法真正与众不同的地方。

turns.en: So Jack, as Spencer alluded to, when you're building a model of retirement outcomes, you have to make a lot of assumptions, not only about markets, but also how people behave. How do you, Spencer and the rest of your team try to make sure that you're making reasonable
turns.zh: Jack，正如Spencer提到的，当你在构建一个退休结果模型时，你必须做很多假设——不仅是关于市场的，还有关于人们如何行为的。当你试图预测退休结果时，你、Spencer以及团队其余人是怎么确保自己在储蓄、退休年龄、社会保障等方面做出合理……

turns.en: assumptions around things like savings, retirement age, social security, et cetera, when you're trying to project retirement outcomes? Well, we're very fortunate when it comes to working with 401K participants. One of the other simulation models we have, not the one that Spencer already talked
turns.zh: ……假设的？嗯，在处理401(k)参与者方面，我们非常幸运。我们还有另一个模拟模型——不是Spencer已经谈过的那个——

turns.en: about, is something that's built literally on millions of participants from thousands of different 401K plans. So when it comes to the ability to actually observe how participants are going to react to various types of plan designs, as well as different types of investment options and
turns.zh: ……它是实打实地建立在来自数千个不同401(k)计划的数百万参与者数据之上的。所以，当谈到能否真正观察参与者会如何对各种类型的计划设计、以及各种类型的投资选项和……做出反应时，

turns.en: different types of markets, we have probably the largest database for that available. In terms of some of the other things that we model, we obviously are able to deal with the Morningstar Capital of Market Assumptions, as well as having a very, very rich database
turns.zh: ……各种类型的市场做出反应——我们大概拥有这方面能拿到的最大数据库。至于我们建模的其他一些内容，我们显然能够用上Morningstar的资本市场假设（Capital Market Assumptions），同时还拥有一个非常非常丰富的……

turns.en: of different household behavior, whether it's during the accumulation stage, or once they retire, and something, I'm sure Spencer's going to get into in more detail later, we're able to do a very, very detailed job looking at what kind of expenses individuals will
turns.zh: ……关于不同家庭行为的数据库，无论是在积累阶段（accumulation stage）还是退休之后。而且有一点——我确信Spencer稍后会详细讲——我们能够非常非常细致地考察个人在退休后会……

turns.en: have in retirement, whether it's just basic consumption, or whether it might be something like long-term care expenses. So let's talk about how people are doing. One topic we've discussed with a number of guests over the years has been whether we have a retirement crisis in the U.S. Spencer, maybe you can talk about what the data actually
turns.zh: ……有哪些支出，是仅仅基本消费，还是可能像长期护理费用这类。那我们来谈谈人们现在的状况。多年来我们跟不少嘉宾讨论过的一个话题是：美国是否存在退休危机。Spencer，也许你可以谈谈数据实际上……

turns.en: tell us about that, are Americans broadly under prepared for retirement, or has the problem concentrated among certain groups? Yeah, thanks for the question, Christine. This is exactly what the Morningstar Model of the U.S. retirement outcomes can answer. We can answer this question.
turns.zh: ……告诉我们什么：美国人整体上是否为退休准备不足，还是这个问题集中在某些群体当中？好，谢谢你提问，Christine。这正是Morningstar美国退休结果模型能回答的问题。我们能回答这个问题。

turns.en: The discussion and discourse in the media on the crisis, I do think there's very clear perspectives. We fall somewhere, I think, somewhere in the middle. We do think there are very clearly groups of people who our model is showing are under prepared, higher rates of retirement income inadequacy. So there is a concentration.
turns.zh: 关于这场危机，媒体上的讨论和话语确实有非常鲜明的立场。我觉得我们大概落在中间某处。我们确实认为，有一批人——我们的模型显示他们准备不足、退休收入不足率（retirement income inadequacy）更高。所以确实存在集中现象。

turns.en: We do see it among people, lower income workers, single women, black and Hispanic households, groups such as these, where there's a higher likelihood of running short of money. Our overall status cool model shows that about 40 to 45% of the populations at risk of
turns.zh: 我们确实在这些人群中看到它：低收入劳动者、单身女性、黑人和西班牙裔家庭——这类群体钱不够用的可能性更高。我们整体的现状（status quo）模型显示，大约40%到45%的人口面临……

turns.en: shortfalls, so a pretty sizable number, that being said, what we did find in our research is that those who are consistently saving. So in our framework, we simulate people saving and participating in a plan, regularly saving over time. The people who follow those paths tend to be in pretty good shape, so participating in
turns.zh: ……资金短缺的风险，这是个相当大的数字。话虽如此，我们在研究中确实发现，那些持续储蓄的人——在我们的框架里，我们模拟人们储蓄、参与计划、长期定期储蓄——走这条路径的人往往状况相当不错。所以，参与……

turns.en: a plan, saving whatever that looks like for a worker, that can help quite a lot, I think pre-intuitively, just the power of compounding and putting money aside. An interesting finding that I thought I'd mention here is that Gen Z workers in our status cool analysis, they're looking a little bit better than some of the later, or I should
turns.zh: ……一个计划、按一个劳动者力所能及的方式去储蓄，这能帮上大忙。我想这几乎是直觉性的——就是复利的力量、把钱存起来的力量。这里我想提一个有意思的发现：在我们的现状分析中，Z世代（Gen Z）劳动者看起来比一些较晚、或者说……

turns.en: say older, age cohorts, where there was more disruption in terms of going from the DB to the DC system. So with Gen Z workers, as more DC plans and accesses there, we're actually seeing lower rates of retirement income inadequacy with Gen Z. One last thing I wanted to highlight here is that long-term care cost has a really, really
turns.zh: ……较年长的年龄群体要好一些——那些群体在从DB（固定收益养老金）向DC（固定缴款计划）体系转轨时经历了更多扰动。所以对Z世代劳动者来说，随着更多DC计划和准入渠道出现，我们实际上看到Z世代的退休收入不足率更低。这里我想强调的最后一点是：长期护理成本对这些数字有着非常非常……

turns.en: big impact on these numbers, and so just to kind of help people, as you kind of see this discourse in the media, long-term care is a really big impact. If you ignore long-term care costs, we published a piece where we did this, and our estimates from that 40 to 45% number came down to around 25%, so a really big impact.
turns.zh: ……大的影响。所以，当你在媒体上看到这些讨论时，我想帮大家理解一点：长期护理的影响非常大。如果你把长期护理成本忽略掉——我们发表过一篇文章就是这么做的——那我们从40%到45%这个数字得出的估计会降到大约25%，所以影响真的很大。

turns.en: Do you think it makes sense to incorporate this a lot of uncertainty with long-term care? It's a very big issue that I think can't speak enough about it, just to being prepared and educate people on that risk. Yeah, we want to delve more into that, Spencer, but sticking with retirement crisis and
turns.zh: 你觉得把长期护理这种高度不确定性纳入进来合理吗？这是一个非常大的问题，我觉得怎么强调都不为过——就是要让人们有所准备、并就这种风险进行教育。是的，我们想再多深入谈谈这点，Spencer，但先紧扣退休危机和……

turns.en: retirement preparedness, we hear a lot about today's economy being kind of a K-shape, where people who have market exposure have done really well, they're out there spending and then lower economic strata, not participating in that. Do you see that in terms of retirement preparedness as well?
turns.zh: ……退休准备度。我们经常听到今天的经济有点像「K型」——那些有市场敞口（market exposure）的人做得非常好，他们在外面消费；而较低经济阶层则没有参与进来。在退休准备度方面，你也看到这种情况吗？

turns.en: Definitely, that's something that in our behavior estimates or our assumptions that Jack was kind of talking through, you do see that the likelihood of participating or saving into an IRA or participating in retirements, employer-sponsored plan for lower income
turns.zh: 当然。这正是Jack刚才讲到的、我们在行为估计或假设里体现的东西：你确实会看到，对于低收入……

turns.en: workers, as an example, it tends to be less than higher income, middle income workers, and so that dynamic definitely is at play. It's something that does help inform our estimates of lower income workers, those pretty good chance they could run short of money.
turns.zh: ……劳动者来说，他们参与IRA储蓄、或参与雇主发起的退休计划的可能性，往往低于高收入、中等收入的劳动者，所以这种动态确实在起作用。它也帮助我们形成对低收入劳动者的估计——这些人钱不够用的可能性相当大。

turns.en: That's also what I think is part of the motivation behind some of the policies that we've seen that have come across our desk that are trying to get universal market participation or universal in U.S. workers participating in the market. That's exactly the thought behind that where folks who traditionally may not have access
turns.zh: 我觉得这也是我们看到的一些政策的动机之一——那些送到我们案头的政策，试图实现普遍的市场参与，让全美劳动者都参与市场。这正是其背后的思路：让那些传统上可能没有渠道……

turns.en: to an advisor, may not be saving, may not really prioritize that, can kind of start and then start building equity and try to kind of help out an upfront. So it is something that we see, and it's something that there's policy initiatives that are going to try to address that, and so we'll see how that plays out.
turns.zh: ……接触到顾问、可能没在储蓄、可能也没把这件事排在优先位置的人，能够起步，然后开始积累权益、并试着从一开始就帮上一把。所以这确实是我们看到的现象，也有一些政策举措打算去解决它，我们就拭目以待结果如何。

turns.en: So when you're evaluating those types of policy initiatives, what type of criteria do you think policy makers and researchers should use to determine whether a proposal actually improves retirement outcomes and long-term retirement security? And I start by bifurcating between Social Security Form, which I'm sure is going to be on the
turns.zh: 那么，当你们评估这类政策举措时，你觉得政策制定者和研究者应该用什么样的标准，来判断一个提案是否真的改善了退休结果和长期退休保障？我会先把它分成两块：一块是社会保障改革——我相信它一定会排在……

turns.en: top of most people's lists of things they want to talk about soon and just general retirement by end proposals. So if it's a letter, if we're not talking about Social Security Form, I think the thing that people have to keep in mind when a proposal comes up is that access has to come first. After that, you can talk about participation,

turns.zh: ……面向Natixis的演讲，在9月份，开始针对一些真实的计划数据来考察这其中的部分内容。但同样，这类情形会因你不同的计划参与者群体而产生巨大差异。不过总体而言，我认为我们能用我们的模型做出相当不错的……

turns.en: trying to show what the distributions are going to look like. We can do stylized examples in our publications, but I think the thing that you really want to focus on is look at your actual planned participant information and run them through models like this and see how much of a
turns.zh: ……工作，去显示这些分布会长什么样。我们可以在出版物里做典型化的例子，但我认为你真正该聚焦的是：查看你实际的计划参与者信息，把他们放进这样的模型里跑一跑，看看能带来多大的……

turns.en: difference it can make. And again, especially if you want to focus on what I would consider your at risk population, those individuals who under the current plan design probably are not going to have sufficient retirement income when they finally retire to basically look at how much impact
turns.zh: ……差异。而且，尤其如果你想聚焦于我认为的「你的高风险人群（at-risk population）」——那些在当前计划设计下、最终退休时很可能没有足够退休收入的个人——去看看仅仅通过改变……

turns.en: you can have on that at risk population just by changing some of these planned design variables. And I think in many cases, the plans we work with there's been a very dramatic impact on that at risk population. So I wanted to follow up on the system that we have for 401Ks where to my mind,
turns.zh: ……这些计划设计变量中的一部分，你能对那批高风险人群产生多大的影响。我认为在很多情况下，对我们合作的那些计划而言，这对高风险人群产生了非常显著的影响。那我想追问一下我们现行的401(k)体系，在我看来，

turns.en: it's pretty inefficient and that each of these companies are trying to sort it out and sometimes, you know, a smaller company might have the same person who's administering payroll also overseeing the 401K plan. So how do we deal with that fact that some companies just aren't in a position to
turns.zh: ……它相当低效，每家公司都在试图自己理顺，有时候，一家较小的公司可能是同一个人在管发工资、同时也在管401(k)计划。那么，我们该如何应对这样一个事实：有些公司就是没有条件去……

turns.en: make good decisions about what's best for their participants? I'll jump in, Jack. It's a great question, Christine, very fair point. Many companies are positioned to do this and I think this is where policymakers are trying to step in and find a way to close the coverage gap, you know,
turns.zh: ……为参与者的最大利益做出好的决定？Jack，我先来接这个问题。这是个好问题，Christine，非常在理。很多公司其实并不具备这样做的条件，我认为这正是政策制定者试图介入、想办法弥合覆盖缺口（coverage gap）的地方，

turns.en: get more people into plans, but while making it less burdensome, you know, the goal is to not make every employer have to figure out all the details of setting up a plan, you want to find a way to kind of, you know, lower the friction here. And so some of the policy proposals that have come out
turns.zh: ……让更多人进入计划，同时又让这件事负担更轻。目标是不必让每一个雇主都得去搞清楚设立一个计划的所有细节，你想办法去降低这里的摩擦。所以最近出台的一些政策提案……

turns.en: recently have been focusing on this. A recent one was the Retirement Savings for Americans Act, which would introduce a federal, through savings like plan into the industry and to, you know, workers who are not covered by an employer would be defaulted into that plan. There are other
turns.zh: ……一直聚焦于此。最近的一个是《Retirement Savings for Americans Act》（美国人的退休储蓄法案），它会向这个行业引入一个联邦层面的、类似节俭储蓄计划（Thrift Savings Plan-like）的方案，让那些没有被雇主计划覆盖的劳动者被默认纳入该计划。还有其他……

turns.en: similar proposals, at least in theme, you know, the auto individual retirement account proposal from Richie Neal. This has been an ongoing focus of policymakers to make something, you know, put something in place so that workers can be put into the system where there's not necessarily
turns.zh: ……类似的提案，至少在主题上类似，比如Richie Neal提出的自动个人退休账户（auto IRA）提案。这一直是政策制定者持续关注的重点：建立起某种机制，让劳动者能被纳入体系，即便不一定……

turns.en: the employer. State auto IRAs does a good number of states now that actually have a state managed plan that, you know, workers who are not covered by a plan at their job can be put into state plan and participate. And so that's kind of the angle that policymakers have taken. We're finding
turns.zh: ……有雇主来承担。州级自动IRA——现在有不少州真的设立了州管理的计划，让那些工作单位没有计划覆盖的劳动者，可以被纳入州计划并参与。所以这就是政策制定者采取的角度：我们在想办法……

turns.en: ways to, you know, make sure people who are not covered, you know, think like gig workers, people are just not going to be in a situation where, you know, the employer is going to have a plan for them to make sure that they're participating. Anything that you want to add on there, Jack?
turns.zh: ……确保那些没有被覆盖的人——比如零工（gig workers），那些所处的境况注定不会有雇主为他们提供计划的人——也能确保他们参与进来。Jack，这方面你有什么要补充的吗？

turns.en: Well, again, I'm not quite sure what we're talking about as far as participant size when it's considered to be a small plan, but I think the more we get into the whole concept of personalization with respect to these plans, whether it's through managed accounts or custom TDFs or what have you,
turns.zh: 嗯，同样，我不太确定我们在参与者规模上所说的「小计划」到底指多大。但我认为，我们越是深入这些计划的「个性化」（personalization）这一整套概念——无论是通过管理账户（managed accounts）、定制的目标日期基金（custom TDFs），还是别的什么——

turns.en: I think we're getting into a situation where just from economies of scale, we're going to have a situation that's going to be more affordable for the small and medium size employers to be able to customize that plan design. I know everyone is going to say, well, AI is going to take care of
turns.zh: ……我认为我们就在走向这样一种局面：仅仅靠规模经济（economies of scale），就会让中小雇主更能负担得起去定制自己的计划设计。我知道大家都会说：AI会搞定……

turns.en: all this, but until we find out what AI can actually do for plan design, I think it's a situation where there are situations available now for the small and medium size employer that can basically have the advantage of companies that have gone through this on moss to basically be able to
turns.zh: ……这一切，但在我们弄清AI究竟能为计划设计做什么之前，我认为当下已经有一些现成的方案，能让中小雇主基本上享有那些已经大规模走过这条路的公司所拥有的优势，从而能够……

turns.en: break out what kind of plan designs would be best for the employer. And then more importantly, once the employer has the plan designed for the employee, how to optimize what the employee should be doing within that plan. So one big issue that's very difficult for retirees, even if they've
turns.zh: ……拆解出什么样的计划设计对雇主最好。然后更重要的是，一旦雇主为员工设计好了计划，如何优化员工在这个计划内应该做的事。有一个大问题对退休人员来说非常棘手，即便他们……

turns.en: been diligent and successful in building up a nest egg for retirement is figuring out how to put together a retirement spending strategy or figuring out how to spend down those assets efficiently after spending, you know, hopefully most of their working lives building up retirement savings.
turns.zh: ……一直勤勉而成功地积累起了一笔退休「金蛋」（nest egg），要想弄明白如何拼凑出一套退休支出策略，或者如何在花了大半辈子职业生涯积累退休储蓄之后、高效地把这些资产花掉，也是件难事。

turns.en: Are there any good solutions out there that you've seen that you think can help retirees with that problem? It is a very tricky, tricky thing to figure out dehumulation. You know, comparing it to accumulation, it's there's a clear direction. You want to save more, just stay invested,
turns.zh: 有没有你见过的、你认为能帮助退休人员解决这个问题的好方案？要搞清楚提取（decumulation）这件事，是非常非常棘手的。你知道，跟积累相比，积累有个明确的方向：你要多存钱、保持投资、

turns.en: diversify, but there is just a lot of uncertainty. In our work, there are various solutions that we have looked at around spending. If you'll humor me as an actuary, there are, of course, self-initization schemes, which I'm referring to, modern tontines, annuities. This is where you're pooling people's
turns.zh: ……分散投资，但其中就是存在大量不确定性。在我们的工作中，我们考察过围绕支出的各种方案。请允许我这个精算师啰嗦一句：当然有所谓「自偿化」（self-annuitization）方案——我指的是现代tontine（联合养老）、年金。这类方案的思路是把大家的钱汇集到一起，

turns.en: money and you're been able to spend it more efficiently. That's the kind of idea. In practice, that's going to be hard to use across the, you know, for everyone out there, given they're not always available. There's a lot of confusion. So I think kind of the way that I look at this
turns.zh: ……从而能更高效地把钱花出去，大致就是这个思路。但在实践中，要让外面所有人都用上它会很难，因为它们并不总是可获得，而且存在大量困惑。所以我认为，我在所有工作中看待这件事的方式是：

turns.en: with all my work is that, you know, to explore different solutions that may help mitigate against longevity risk such as annuities that can be a part of a plan. But overall, you know, having a very adaptive process to planning, I think is really, really important here. Lifespan is uncertain. That's
turns.zh: ……去探索那些可能有助于缓解长寿风险（longevity risk）的不同方案，比如年金可以作为计划的一部分。但总体而言，拥有一个非常有适应性（adaptive）的规划过程，我认为在这里真的非常非常重要。寿命是不确定的，这……

turns.en: something that's hard to know. Market rates are of course uncertain. Needs that come up, you know, long-term care I mentioned earlier. That's uncertain. So just treating this as an adaptive process and knowing that, you know, you've tested different things in your planning when shocks come, when,
turns.zh: ……是难以预知的。市场利率当然是不确定的。冒出来的各种需求——比如我前面提到的长期护理——也是不确定的。所以就把这当成一个有适应性的过程，并且知道：你已经在规划中测试过各种情形，这样当冲击来临、当……

turns.en: you know, when things happen, you have an adjustment that you can make.
turns.zh: ……当事情发生时，你有一个可以做出的调整。

turns.en: So I wanted to follow up on the annuity comment and Spencer, maybe you can talk about the role of annuities within 401k plans. We've seen target date series adding series that include annuities. What's your take on that whole trend? Great question, Christine. This is right up my alley.
turns.zh: 那我想追问一下刚才关于年金的说法。Spencer，也许你可以谈谈年金在401(k)计划内部的角色。我们看到目标日期系列（target date series）正在加入包含年金的产品系列。你怎么看这整个趋势？好问题，Christine，这正对我的路子。

turns.en: annuities in 401k plans, you know, I do think there's value there. I think they can be helpful to plan participants. There are a lot of people who could use, I think, some more exposure to mitigate longevity risk to a larger extent. I do think a lot of people, you know, it's difficult
turns.zh: 401(k)计划里的年金，我确实认为其中有价值，我认为它们能对计划参与者有帮助。我觉得有很多人可以更多地借助它，在更大程度上缓解长寿风险。我确实认为，对很多人来说……这很难，

turns.en: within the fine contribution plan space in terms of making sure you have the right type of plan to use this solution. So you're really looking for plans where a lot of people have, you know, there's a meaningful number of people in the retirement with sufficient balances to convert
turns.zh: ……在固定缴款计划这个领域里，难在要确保你拥有合适类型的计划来用这个方案。所以你真正要找的，是那种有大量人、有相当数量临近退休、且余额足以把……

turns.en: that savings into something that's meaningful in terms of an income stream from the annuity. You know, I think you kind of need lower turnover. These solutions are designed where you've kind of build up an income balance as you hit, you know, your 50s, you build up an income balance
turns.zh: ……储蓄转换成来自年金的、有意义的收入流的计划。你知道，我觉得你需要较低的换手率（turnover）。这类方案的设计是这样的：当你到了50多岁，你逐步积累起一个「收入余额」（income balance），

turns.en: so that when you're in your 60s, you have something meaningful. So you kind of need some things to line up from the employer for the plan. But I do think they can be pretty valuable. annuities in general, you know, I have researched on this topic. They can be an effective fixed income substitute,
turns.zh: ……这样等你到了60多岁，你就有了有意义的东西。所以你需要雇主和计划这边有一些条件凑齐。但我确实认为它们可能相当有价值。总体而言，年金——我研究过这个课题——可以是一种有效的固定收益替代品，

turns.en: you know, it is a personalized thing to look through from a, you know, person's actual circumstances, what other exposures they have to lifetime income, you know, a pension plan. We've talked about social security, but of course, social security still is in play here. So I do think they can be valuable,
turns.zh: ……不过这是一件很个性化的事，要从一个人的实际境况去看：他们还有哪些终身收入（lifetime income）的敞口，比如养老金计划。我们谈过社会保障，当然，社会保障在这里依然是变量之一。所以我确实认为它们可以很有价值，

turns.en: but it is something that is is hard to deploy in the industry and you've got to be very careful with, you know, where you use this. But the research does show, you know, my research, all the research that there's value to participants to use these solutions in retirement outcomes.
turns.zh: ……但它在行业里确实难以部署，你必须非常小心在什么地方使用它。不过研究确实表明——我的研究、所有研究——参与者在退休结果上使用这些方案是有价值的。

turns.en: So earlier in the discussion, we touched on the issue of long-term care, which is really one of the biggest and most uncertain expenses that retirees might face. How can advisors incorporate long-term care costs into retirement planning without either understating the risk
turns.zh: 在前面讨论中，我们谈到了长期护理的问题，它真的是退休人员可能面临的最大、最不确定的开销之一。顾问该如何把长期护理成本纳入退休规划，既不小看这个风险，

turns.en: or assuming that every retiree will face extremely high costs for long-term care?
turns.zh: ……也不假设每一位退休人员都会面临极高的长期护理费用？

turns.en: With long-term care, I think it, it's something that I think has to be addressed with scenario or sensitivity analysis. I think Jack kind of highlighted this earlier for social security reform, but this definitely applies for long-term care. There's not, you know, one number that I would just
turns.zh: 关于长期护理，我认为它必须用情景分析（scenario analysis）或敏感性分析（sensitivity analysis）来处理。我想Jack之前在社会保障改革上也强调过这点，但这绝对同样适用于长期护理。并不存在某一个数字，是我可以直接……

turns.en: plug in and use, you can know, I think it does vary by person, by gender, by income level, wealth, all these things can impact how likely it is to need long-term care. And so I think the best course of action is sensitivity testing. I do think people should think through or talk with
turns.zh: ……填进去就用的。我觉得它确实因人而异、因性别而异、因收入水平、财富而异，所有这些都会影响一个人需要长期护理的可能性。所以我认为最佳做法是敏感性测试（sensitivity testing）。我确实认为人们应该想清楚，或者跟……

turns.en: your advisor, you know, it's impossible to know in advance what type of care you might need, but I think it's still very good to have preferences and have thought out, you know, a nursing home versus home health care, other arrangements, family support, that's something that, you know, could be
turns.zh: ……你的顾问谈谈。你不可能提前知道自己可能需要哪种类型的护理，但我认为，事先有偏好、想清楚还是很好的——比如养老院还是居家护理（home health care）、其他安排、家人支持，这些都是可以……

turns.en: thought through in terms of cost estimates. It's a tricky endeavor, but, you know, you kind of want to play around with the different levers and understand, you know, what the cost could be. In practice, a lot of people do spend down a Medicaid, and so thinking through that, you know,
turns.zh: ……在成本估算方面想清楚的。这是一件棘手的事，但你会想去摆弄不同的杠杆、了解成本可能是多少。实践中，很多人确实会把资产花到符合Medicaid（医疗补助）资格为止，所以把这点想清楚，

turns.en: with wealth levels, with what, you know, an investor or a client has, thinking through if that approach should be taken, and of course, there's a whole dedicated space in the planning world, Medicaid spend down and strategy there. So it is something that I think is tricky.
turns.zh: ……结合财富水平、结合投资者或客户实际拥有的资产，去思考是否该采取那种路径。当然，在规划界有一整个专门的领域，就是Medicaid资产耗尽（spend-down）及其策略。所以我认为这是一件棘手的事。

turns.en: In the end, sensitivity testing is, I think, the best way to approach this. One last point I want to mention on long-term care, we do have a study that will be not a specific publication date yet, but we're looking at long-term care insurance,
turns.zh: 归根结底，我认为敏感性测试是处理这件事的最佳方式。关于长期护理，我想提的最后一点是：我们确实有一项研究——还没有具体的发表日期——我们在考察长期护理保险（long-term care insurance），

turns.en: including combination insurance products. So, you know, whole life or universal life with long-term care or an annuity with long-term care, that's something that we're studying. So, you know, interested to see how that might be helpful for folks as they navigate long-term care risk.
turns.zh: ……包括组合型保险产品。比如带长期护理的终身寿险（whole life）或万能寿险（universal life），或者带长期护理的年金，这些都是我们在研究的。所以我很想看看，这些在人们应对长期护理风险时能有多大的帮助。

turns.en: Well, Spencer, and Jack, you two worked on some research. I think it was published last year that basically concluded that a lot of the retirement planning research does not adequately factor in long-term care. That it's a bigger issue for more households than many researchers
turns.zh: Spencer、Jack，你们俩做过一些研究，我记得是去年发表的，基本上得出结论：很多退休规划研究没有充分把长期护理纳入考量；对更多家庭来说，它是一个比许多研究者……

turns.en: are assuming. Can you talk about that? Absolutely. Long-term care, it's a divisive topic. It's something that a lot of families in practice will use Medicaid, will, you know, rely on family support. And so, you know, if you look at different data sources, you may not see
turns.zh: ……所假设的更大的问题。你们能谈谈吗？当然可以。长期护理是一个有争议的话题。实践中，很多家庭会用Medicaid、会依靠家人支持。所以如果你去看不同的数据源，你也许看不到……

turns.en: really high costs for every family, even though a lot of people in those families need long-term care, but are getting unpaid care from their family, you know, spouse or, you know, children, that's a very common occurrence where that's not going to be built into
turns.zh: ……每个家庭都有非常高的成本，尽管这些家庭里很多人需要长期护理，但他们得到的是来自家人——配偶或子女——的无偿照护。这是一种非常普遍的情况，而它不会被纳入……

turns.en: a framework because a cost is not, you know, you don't see a dollar cost put into, you know, in the data. Our approach here is we take, you know, in our analysis, we have a long-term care, you know, framework that will simulate how likely it is that someone will need long-term care
turns.zh: ……一个框架里，因为这里没有成本——你在数据里看不到一个以美元计的成本被填进去。我们的做法是：在我们的分析里，我们有一个长期护理框架，用来模拟某个人需要长期护理的可能性，

turns.en: in different types of long-term care. This framework is based on the health and retirement study, so that study tracks, you know, individual people and spouse over a period of time as they kind of enter retirements, so both retirements and different health factors, including, you know,
turns.zh: ……以及需要哪些不同类型的长期护理。这个框架基于健康与退休研究（Health and Retirement Study），该研究会在一段时间里追踪个人及其配偶，看他们如何逐步进入退休，既包括退休，也包括不同的健康因素，其中就有……

turns.en: need of long-term care. And so, we built it based on that framework, and we simulate needing care, and then we use the generous cost of care assumptions with adjustments to model the cost. And so, that's our approach to look at how likely it is someone might need long-term care and privately
turns.zh: ……长期护理的需求。所以我们基于那个框架来搭建，模拟「需要照护」的情形，然后采用Genworth的照护成本假设并加以调整，来对成本建模。这就是我们的做法：考察某个人需要长期护理、并自费……

turns.en: fund it. We think that's the best kind of way to think about it, because then if you start assuming, you know, family can take care of it, you know, you assume away a large cost that otherwise, you know, the household would have had to have paid. So, that's our approach with
turns.zh: ……自费承担它的可能性。我们认为这是思考它最好的方式，因为如果你开始假设「家人能搞定」，你就把一笔巨大的成本假设掉了，而那本来是家庭不得不支付的。所以这就是我们在……

turns.en: long-term care, but we do run it in our framework multiple ways, you know, we do have a Medicaid functionality built-in where, you know, if people qualify based on accident income limits, they could get Medicaid support for long-term care can definitely have a big, you know,
turns.zh: ……长期护理上的做法。不过我们在框架里确实用多种方式运行它。我们内置了一个Medicaid功能：如果人们符合基于资产与收入上限的条件，他们就能获得Medicaid对长期护理的支持——这当然会对……

turns.en: impact on surviving spouse or the non-affected spouse. So, we modeled this different ways, but in general, it's a very tricky thing to kind of incorporate into the discussion since there's a lot of different perspectives that kind of go into it. I agree with everything Spencer said,
